clue.text: Drink cider, as broke

indicators.note: something broke is smashed up, so the letters of these two words are reassembled

explanation.surface: An order to drink cider because the speaker is short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like a description of a penniless drinker, but it tells you to rearrange CIDER AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Plug sport and PE perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be in another order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether games and gym lessons could be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange SPORT plus PE; PE is physical education, the school gym lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopper is a bung that closes the neck of a bottle, which is a plug.

clue.text: Speed back East with a marine

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word speed from right to left

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone hurries back eastwards accompanied by a Royal Marine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marine' looks like a soldier but is the adjective defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-sea describes life or activity in the ocean depths, which is marine.

clue.text: List canoe usage at the seaside

indicators.note: usage hints that the letters of these words are put to a different use, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of how canoes are used at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'usage' is the rearrangement signal for LIST CANOE; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastline is the shore where land meets sea, the seaside.

clue.text: Withdraw troops over a wide area

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, that is above, the second

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a body of British army troops
a tract is a large expanse of land

explanation.surface: An army pulls its soldiers back across a broad region.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, sits over TRACT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or pull in, which is to withdraw.

clue.text: Relevant article for personnel officers

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
pro means in favour of, for
POs are petty officers, naval personnel of officer rank

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written for the staff in charge of human resources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'personnel officers' suggests HR managers, but gives POs, petty officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means pertinent to the matter in hand, so relevant.

clue.text: Old soldiers well-used to pulling strings!

definitions.text: Old soldiers well-used to pulling strings!

parts.words: Old soldiers well-used to pulling strings!
parts.note: pulling strings suggests wire-pulling influence, but these old soldiers drew the strings of their bows

explanation.surface: Veteran soldiers are adept at using influence behind the scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling strings' normally means exerting influence; here it is literal, drawing a bowstring.
explanation.definitionFit: Archers were bowmen in medieval armies, soldiers who drew bowstrings.

clue.text: Stormed at for getting into debt

indicators.note: getting into tells you one piece goes inside another

parts.note: being in debt is being in the red, so red stands for debt
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone raged because they had fallen into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: AT goes inside RED, from the phrase 'in the red' meaning in debt. 'Stormed' here is the old verb rate, to scold angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is an old word for scolding them furiously, so rated means raged or ranted.

clue.text: The left capturing a number would be a forewarning

indicators.note: capturing means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Political left-wingers seizing a figure would be an omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The left' sounds political but is PORT, a ship's left side, which takes TEN inside; 'would be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen or sign of something to come, a forewarning.

clue.text: Wrestle possibly to perspire profusely

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged differently, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Wrestling might make you sweat heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells you to rearrange WRESTLE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To swelter is to be oppressively hot and sweat heavily.

clue.text: Ham on the turn

parts.note: on and over can both mean above or upon
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: Some ham on the point of going bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' suggests food going off, but splits into OVER and ACT (a stage turn).
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated way, which is to overact.

clue.text: The party about to return by water

parts.note: c, for circa, means about

indicators.note: return means the word to is read backwards

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes, a body of water

explanation.surface: A group is about to head back by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) plus OT, the reversal signalled by 'return', then Lake ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group of people, a party or set.

clue.text: Assume one is in the mail

indicators.note: is in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the post is the mail
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone supposes a letter is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: I (one) is put in POST.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a basis for argument, to suppose.

clue.text: A qualification men met — and otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reservation that the men encountered, and something else besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' tells you to rearrange MEN MET AND.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change that modifies a statement, a qualification of it.

clue.text: Individual with a pragmatic attitude where a catalogue's concerned

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A practical person when it comes to drawing up inventories.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (regarding) plus A LIST; 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist accepts things as they are and deals with them practically.

clue.text: There's confusion about the trainee's protection

indicators.note: about means going round another piece
confusion means a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, so it stands for a trainee

explanation.surface: Confusion surrounds the trainee's safety cover.
explanation.walkthrough: THERE'S jumbled (signalled by 'confusion') gives SHETER, which goes about L, the learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place or structure giving cover, a protection.

clue.text: Cultivation?

parts.note: cultivating soil is literally labour on the ground, though the word names a raised bank of soil

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, ground labour; as one word it is a defensive bank.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthwork is an embankment of soil; tilling land is, punningly, labour on the ground.

clue.text: Sent a goody-goody inside — so wise

indicators.note: inside places the second piece within the first

parts.note: pi is short for pious, describing a goody-goody

explanation.surface: A prig has been dispatched to the inner area, which was clever.
explanation.walkthrough: A PI goes inside SENT; PI is crossword shorthand for pious; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means having great wisdom, so wise.

clue.text: Point out to a mad character causing split

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
the Mad Hatter is the madcap host of the tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Pointing out a crazy person causes a rift.
explanation.walkthrough: S (south) plus HATTER, from 'mad as a hatter'; 'out to a' and 'causing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break into pieces, to split apart.

clue.text: Questioning the little page getting dressed up

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page
robing is putting on ceremonial robes

explanation.surface: Interrogating a small pageboy who is dressing up.
explanation.walkthrough: P (page) plus ROBING.
explanation.definitionFit: Probing means searching and inquiring closely, as in questioning.

clue.text: One believes the way lies in more sound

indicators.note: lies in means one piece rests inside another

parts.note: truer means more accurate or more sound
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A trusting person thinks the path lies in better noise.
explanation.walkthrough: ST (street) goes inside TRUER.
explanation.definitionFit: A truster is one who places faith or belief in someone.

clue.text: Resolve to take some exercise

definitions.meaning: to resolve a problem is to settle or solve it
to train physically at a gym

explanation.surface: A decision to go and get fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Work out can mean solve a puzzle or settle a matter, and also to do physical training.

clue.text: Finally deals with cranks

definitions.meaning: turns a handle, as when tightening a clock spring

explanation.surface: Someone at last handles the eccentrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind up means bring to an end, and also turn a crank to tighten a spring.

clue.text: Rings about train crash in Canada

indicators.note: about means the rings go round the other letters

parts.note: o is ring-shaped, so two rings give two Os

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Bells ring after a railway accident in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: Two Os go about NTARI, the jumble of TRAIN signalled by 'crash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a province in Canada.

clue.text: Everything in a trial that's most incredible

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a test is a trial
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything in a court case is utterly unbelievable.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL goes in TEST; 'that's' is a link. 'Tallest' as in a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is far-fetched, so the tallest is the hardest to believe.

clue.text: The drill-sergeant's revolutionary order

parts.note: revolutionary suggests rebellion but means turning round, a parade-ground command

explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests rebellion but describes a command to turn round to face the opposite way.
explanation.definitionFit: On parade, the command to reverse direction makes soldiers turn to face the rear.

clue.text: Pay for leading two of trumps and scoff

indicators.note: leading two of takes the opening pair of letters of the next word

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A card player pays for leading two trumps and then mocks.
explanation.walkthrough: TR, the first two letters of 'trumps', plus EAT; 'scoff' means gobble, not mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone is to pay for their food or drink.

clue.text: Being enthusiastic, the Spanish are building

parts.note: hot on something means keen or enthusiastic
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Keen on things, the Spaniards are constructing something.
explanation.walkthrough: HOT plus EL; 'Being' and 'are' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a building providing lodging for guests.

clue.text: Taken in hand by the main supervisor

definitions.text: Taken in hand by the main supervisor

parts.words: Taken in hand by the main supervisor
parts.note: the main is the sea, and its supervisor is the sea god who carries a three-pronged spear

explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the sea, so its supervisor is Neptune, who holds a three-pronged spear.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune, ruler of the sea, is always shown holding a three-pronged spear.

clue.text: Beat the top man in the rush

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush
CO is a commanding officer, the top man

explanation.surface: The boss was struck in the stampede.
explanation.walkthrough: CO goes in SURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To scourge is to whip, to beat severely.

clue.text: He sets all straight-it's not left to the queen

parts.note: the opposite of left is right
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A fixer says it's not left to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: RIGHT plus ER (Elizabeth Regina); 'it's' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A righter is one who rights wrongs, putting things straight.

clue.text: Appear morose about fine project

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Appear morose about fine project (4,3)'. POUT round OK gives POKOUT, an E short of POKEOUT; no clue word supplies the E, so the clue as held looks misread or wrong
